replies.author: 69Trash420Panda
replies.body: Because he’s doing it the hard way. Multi image to 3d mesh generators exist and are very very good. I’ve been generating war planes with 1.5 mil faces for free, 5 min each fully textured.

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body: That's true. This "hard way" is a technique called box modeling and it's useful in creating intricate low poly models and when creating detailed objects that require high technical accuracy. AI's are still pretty bad at this.

replies.author: 69Trash420Panda
replies.body: You can run a reptology model or whatever it’s called to turn high poly into low poly models. Start with 50k faces gen and then use other model to make it low poly 😊

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body: Yes you can, but you don't  really need to do it. It's just one technique for making a game ready model. High poly model is only needed if you are baking detail from it to low poly version of it.

comments.author: shayeryan
comments.body: I found it to be pretty good at structural rigid things like this, guns, buildings etc. But not so great at organic things like plants. Did you give it a reference image first? That seems to really speed things up with better end product.

replies.body: Yeah, I probably should’ve just given it reference images from the start. At the very end, it kept making the windshield rounded, and no matter how many times I told it to make it square, it wouldn’t listen. comments.author: Interesting-Bee-113
comments.body:
I spend so so so much time trying to get Opus to model a rally car for me.

It was pretty bad and never once could we reliably make any directed corrections

I ended up deciding that actually modeling it by hand would be better and faster some how.

replies.author: CryoNigiri_
replies.body: Yeah, exactly. It used to be basically useless for this. Opus 5 seems way better at spatial reasoning though, and that’s what really surprised me this time.
